title: Earlier Delivery-Charge Refunds and the Wrong Item Claims Delivery Refund
content:
Refund Operations ruling for Delivery Claims: on a Wrong Item Claim, the wrong-shipment repeat share follows the delivery-charge refunds already paid to the customer under delivery claims.

**Rule.** The wrong-shipment repeat share depends on the delivery-charge refunds already paid under delivery claims on the customer's orders: counting the order-level refunds with reason delivery claim and no order line dated in the trailing 12 calendar months, as they stand on the orders' payment records, two or more pay 50% of the basis, exactly one pays 75%, and none leaves the basis whole.

## What is counted

- Order-level refunds on the payment records of any of the customer's orders.
- Whose reason is delivery claim.
- That name no order line — refunds of a delivery charge, not of merchandise.
- Dated in the 12 calendar months up to today.

| Such refunds counted | Repeat share |
|---|---|
| none | 100% — the basis whole |
| exactly 1 | 75% |
| 2 or more | 50% |

## Cases (hypothetical payment records)

- One delivery-claim refund of 7.95 USD with no order line, 3 months ago: 75%.
- One delivery-claim refund of 7.95 USD with no order line and one delivery-claim refund of 60.00 USD on a dress line, both this year: only the first counts — 75%.
- Two delivery-claim refunds with no order line, 2 and 11 months ago: 50%.
- A single such refund dated 14 months ago: not in the window — 100%.
